summary: Use a helper for `super.prop` reads/writes when JavaScript property descriptors or accessors are observable.

target.notes: Perform JavaScript [[Get]]/[[Set]] starting at the base prototype while using the current this value as Receiver.

caveats: A simple C# `base.Property` can be used only under stronger closed-world accessor conditions; arbitrary JavaScript descriptor behavior requires the helper.
references: ECMAScript Super Calls and Super Property: https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-super-keyword

tests.name: super getter receives derived this
tests.input: class B { get x(){ return this.y; } } class D extends B { constructor(){ super(); this.y=5; } m(){ return super.x; } } console.log(new D().m());

tests.name: edge: super setter writes via receiver
tests.input: class B { set x(v){ this.y=v; } } class D extends B { m(){ super.x=7; } } const d=new D(); d.m(); console.log(d.y);
